expectations.text: Uses the CMMC scoping categories: CUI assets, Security Protection Assets, Contractor Risk Managed Assets, Specialized Assets, and out-of-scope assets — with the required treatment of each
expectations.evidence: Lists the categories but mis-treats Specialized Assets, lumping them with out-of-scope: 'Specialized Assets (IoT, OT, GFE...) and Out-of-Scope Assets: assets with no CUI touchpoint... genuinely excluded' — Specialized Assets are in scope and must be documented

expectations.text: Endorses the enclave strategy: concentrate CUI processing/storage/transmission into a bounded environment to shrink the assessment boundary
expectations.evidence: you isolate the systems, users, and network segments that actually create, store, process, or transmit... CUI into a bounded enclave... your Level 2 assessment scope... only needs to cover the enclave

expectations.text: Requires dataflow mapping: where CUI enters, moves, is stored, and exits (email, file shares, endpoints, cloud)
expectations.evidence: Identify every place CUI enters... Trace where that data is stored, who touches it, what systems process it (engineering tools, ERP, email, file shares, backup systems), and where it exits

expectations.text: Covers external service providers: CSPs handling CUI need FedRAMP Moderate (or equivalency); ESPs/MSPs are in scope via Security Protection Asset treatment
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'GCC High... / equivalent FedRAMP Moderate-or-higher tenant' only as an architecture option; no stated CSP FedRAMP Moderate requirement for CUI, and no ESP/MSP-as-Security-Protection-Asset coverage

expectations.text: Covers flow-down: subcontractors receiving CUI need Level 2; FCI-only subs need Level 1 — with the DFARS 7012 clause flowing down
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'subcontractor flow-down' only as a data exit; no Level 2/Level 1 subcontractor requirements and no DFARS 7012 clause flow-down
